goal: close blocker 1b (on-device weight encoding) and then STEP 3 (the other four SpeechNet convs)
status: PHASES 1-3 COMPLETE (blocks 1-4 bit-exact end to end on device); phase 4 (block 0, BLOCKER 3) open

1.what: NE16WeightEncode kernel + op; weight arrives unencoded as an int8 graph input and is bit-serial encoded on the cluster

2.what: RQSPerturbRademacher -> NE16WeightEncode -> Conv, L+ and L-

4.what: STEP 3b -- block 0, needs the signed-activation fix

encode_cost.covers: L2->L1 DMA of the 2048 B raw int8 weight plus the bit-serial encode of 4096 B, 8 cores
encode_cost.conclusion: negligible -- Option A (device encode) is confirmed over Option B (linearity decomposition)

kernel_validation.method: compiled TargetLibraries/GAP9/src/NE16WeightEncode.c natively and compared against Deeploy's own _weightEncode via ctypes
kernel_validation.result: MATCH on every case -- so phases 3-4 need no new encoder

qzo_weight_path_cost.note: full on-device QZO weight path (perturb + bit-serial encode) costs 2.7% of the layer

L_minus_method: negating the per-channel multiplier is exactly equivalent to negating the Rademacher sign (RandomNoiseQuant.c:31), so L- is testable under the plain inference runner with the neutral perturbation_sign=+1 default. All 2048 weight elements differ between L+ and L-, and the output range moves [-85,60] -> [-82,57], so it is a real second test rather than a relabelling.

step3_blocks.status: BLOCKED on BLOCKER 3 -- activation range [-66,127] is genuinely signed

kx1_fix: Conv1xKTemplate stepped infeat_addr by one PIXEL (ch_im_in bytes), which is only right for 1xK. For Kx1 a tap is one ROW, so the step is the input row stride -- a PER-TILE value (dim_im_in_x_stride), so the template references the substituted variable rather than a constant. Verified in the generated C: block 3 emits `+ 1 * *..._dim_im_in_x_stride_ref` where block 1 emits `+ 1 * 8`.
performance_note: NE16 is 4.3x-6.8x SLOWER than pulp_nn_conv on every block. Correctness of the NE16 path is established; closing the performance gap is STEP 4. The NE16 figures include the on-device perturb+encode (2.7% on block 1) which the cluster reference does not perform.
